opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees max out at write, and admin would require the role to own Payroll (Payroll Specialist), which does not apply. Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E045 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read access, and admin is never allowed. The requested write level for Payroll is above the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two agents' notes conflict on employment type: HR reports E045 as full-time (Engineer), while Security reports E045 as a contractor with basic security training. Per the access policy, a contractor with only basic training maxes out at read and is never granted admin or write; the requested write level is above that maximum, so the maximum of read applies. I am following the Security record for access classification and granting the more restrictive permissible level.
